svg.title: QMSR Inspection-Readiness Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-qmsr-inspection-readiness; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: QMSR Inspection-Readiness Gates; subtitle: Four checks before the February 2, 2026 hard switch bites; caption: The QMSR incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference, makes risk the thread investigators pull, and opens management review and audit records to inspection.; assumptions note: Gate sequence reflects the operator gates attributed below; an ISO or MDSAP certificate does not exempt a firm from any gate.; note: Attributed to AMORIT EDUCATION, Regulatory Compliance Associates, Matrix One, Medmarc, and Greenlight Guru.; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the quality system already built on ISO 13485:2016?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-baseline now; firms complying only with Part 820 face significant change.; gate: G2; question: Does the risk management file reflect the latest complaint trends?; pass next: G3; fail action: Update it before the visit; Matrix One says the risk file steers the inspection.; gate: G3; question: Are procedures free of 'do not show to FDA' language and fewer-CAPA objectives?; pass next: G4; fail action: Sweep and rewrite; management review and audit records are now reviewable.; gate: G4; question: Is every automated label check backed by a statistically significant human sample?; pass next: Ready for a CP 7382.850 inspection; fail action: Add the human sample, as Henry of Greenlight Guru insists.

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Is the quality system already built on ISO 13485:2016?; pass next: G2; fail action: Re-baseline now; firms complying only with Part 820 face significant change.
gate: G2; question: Does the risk management file reflect the latest complaint trends?; pass next: G3; fail action: Update it before the visit; Matrix One says the risk file steers the inspection.

gate: G3; question: Are procedures free of 'do not show to FDA' language and fewer-CAPA objectives?; pass next: G4; fail action: Sweep and rewrite; management review and audit records are now reviewable.

gate: G4; question: Is every automated label check backed by a statistically significant human sample?; pass next: Ready for a CP 7382.850 inspection; fail action: Add the human sample, as Henry of Greenlight Guru insists.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate sequence reflects the operator gates attributed below; an ISO or MDSAP certificate does not exempt a firm from any gate.
